their health was disrupted for a month or more afterward. 39% said their RSV or respiratory virus infections worsened management of their existing health condition. Despite having a higher risk of severe complications from RSVi, 44% said they have not recently discussed it with a healthcare professional. MISSISSAUGA, ON, Nov. 2, 2026 /CNW/ -- New survey findings commissioned by GSK suggest that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other respiratory viruses can significantly disrupt the health and daily lives of Canadian adults living with chronic health conditions, often extending beyond initial infection and making management of their existing condition more challenging. According to the survey, 80% of adults living with certain chronic conditions reported that respiratory viruses such as RSV have impacted their health and daily life, as well as the lives of those around them. Continue Reading New Survey Shows Lasting Impact of RSV on Adults with Chronic Conditions For many respondents, the impact lasted long beyond the initial illness. Among those who had experienced RSV, 39% reported their health was disrupted for a month or more after infection, while 7% said it took more than a year for their health to return to normal, or that it has still not fully returned to normal. The findings also highlight how respiratory viruses can complicate management of existing chronic conditions. Nearly 2 in 5 (39%) respondents reported that their chronic health condition worsened when they experienced a respiratory virus such as RSV. The impact was particularly notable among those living with asthma (54%) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (46%), who reported worsening symptoms during or following infection. Beyond physical health, respondents also reported impacts on mental wellbeing (27%), loss of earnings due to time away from work (22%), and reduced daily independence (22%). Although concern about respiratory viruses is high, conversations about RSV remain limited. While 80% are concerned that respiratory viruses could interfere with management of their condition or worsen symptoms, 44% reported they had not recently discussed RSV with healthcare professional. Survey participants included 1,500 Canadians aged 18 years and over living with one or more of the following chronic health conditions: diabetes (type 1 or type 2), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension.ii "Living with a chronic condition, such as asthma often requires careful day-to-day management. When RSV or another respiratory virus strikes, the effects can extend far beyond a few days of illness," Jeffrey Beach, President & CEO, Asthma Canada. "That's why it's important for people living with chronic health conditions to feel confident speaking with their healthcare professional about RSV and learning the steps they can take to protect their health." Adults living with chronic conditions, including diabetes, asthma, chronic obstructive lung disease (COPD) and heart failure are at increased risk of severe outcomes from RSV.iii More than 90% of adults over 60 who are hospitalized with RSV have at least one chronic health condition.iv,v "These findings highlight an important gap between awareness of risk and the conversations about prevention," said Dr. Michelle Horn, Country Medical Director, GSK Canada. "Many adults living with chronic conditions recognize that respiratory viruses can affect their health and daily lives, yet discussions about RSV are not happening as often as they could. Understanding the potential impact of RSV and speaking with a healthcare professional can help Canadians make informed decisions about their respiratory health." As GSK marks RSV Awareness Week 2026 globally, these findings underscore the importance of helping adults understand the potential impact RSV can have on chronic disease management, daily life and overall wellbeing, while encouraging more proactive conversations with healthcare professionals. About the GSK RSV Awareness Survey The RSV Awareness Canadian Survey is an online survey commissioned and funded by GSK.vi It involved 1,500 adults aged 18 and over, and was conducted between July 15 – August 7, 2026, by Human8, on behalf of GSK.vii The survey comprised eight questions covering RSV awareness, short and long-term disruptions and specific questions for people living with certain long-term conditions.viii This survey aimed to better understand how Canadians living with certain chronic conditions perceive the risk and potential impact of RSV. The survey explored RSV awareness, levels of concern among those at increased risk and whether individuals are proactively discussing RSV and preventative health measures with healthcare professionals. title: 秋冬呼吸道合胞病毒进入活跃期,广州“医院+社区”双通道开放进口长效单抗接种
excerpt: 秋冬季节来临,呼吸道传染病进入高发时段,婴幼儿时期感染率最高的病原体之一、呼吸道合胞病毒也迎来活跃期。10月28日,广州市天河区天园街道社区卫生服务中心全科门诊,一对年轻父母带着出生刚满1个月的宝宝,完成了长效呼吸道合胞病毒单抗——克莱罗韦单抗注射液接种。这也是该单抗作为进口创新一类生物制品落地广州后,在社区接种点的首批接种之一。
